incidents.symptom: Preflight exited 1 before any provider send; stdout was empty and the wrapper received JSONDecodeError while decoding a command result.
incidents.cause: The preflight interpreted the silent runtime-check command output as JSON. The captured traceback confirms JSONDecodeError; the report identifies this as a silent runtime check parsed as JSON.
incidents.verified_fix: Use the authenticated /readyz endpoint for runtime identity and readiness. The repaired preflight completed with READY_ZERO_SEND and preserved baseline DB/service checks.

future.trigger: A readiness or identity helper returns empty output, plain text, or a different schema.
future.readonly_check: Inspect command exit code and stdout shape; call the authenticated readiness endpoint and confirm provider-call counter remains unchanged.
future.preferred_fix: Treat readiness as an explicit structured contract; never parse an unchecked command as JSON.
future.stop: Stop before staging or sending requests if identity/readiness cannot be parsed and baseline state cannot be confirmed.

incidents.symptom: Full Linux image archive transfer hit the 180-second SCP timeout; a partial archive was retained, so the full image was not used for remote deployment.
incidents.cause: Large full-image SCP was too slow for the bounded transfer window; exact network/root cause was not measured.
incidents.cause_confidence: high for timeout; low for underlying transport cause
incidents.verified_fix: Transfer only the two changed source files plus image-export and source-manifest, then build an offline delta image from the existing remote base image. Each delta transfer exited 0; remote file hashes and dependencies were checked.

evidence.note: Section 4 records full-image SCP timeout and retained partial file; no hash recorded for this prose evidence
180-second transfer limit in script; source hash not collected
all four delta transfers exit 0; provider_calls 0
remote delta image verified; provider calls 0

future.trigger: A large immutable image must cross the same constrained remote link.
future.readonly_check: Check archive size/hash, prior base image identity, transfer exit code and remote target size/hash; do not treat a partial SCP artifact as usable.
future.preferred_fix: Prefer source-manifest-verified delta transfer and offline build atop a verified existing base when dependency parity is proven.
future.stop: Stop rollout if any transferred file hash, source manifest, dependency set, or build verification differs.

incidents.symptom: Local Linux image ID sha256:786a6a… differed from ECS image ID sha256:80e2f2… despite the same source commit.
incidents.cause: Report attributes ID difference to build metadata; 508 packaged file hashes and dependency versions matched. This is not evidence of runtime incompatibility, but the ID difference leaves image-level identity non-equivalence.
incidents.cause_confidence: partial: file/dependency parity verified; metadata explanation reported, low-level cause not independently isolated
incidents.failed_attempt: Local image ID equality was not achieved; deployment proceeded with manifest/package verification.
incidents.verified_fix: Verify every packaged application file hash and installed dependency version, and record both image IDs. ECS rollout receipt confirms source commit 29ecf2f5d3037eed99a4de783546dee272a761bd, application update PASS, no provider calls, and DB/Redis unchanged.

evidence.note: local Linux image ID, 508 files and dependency parity
remote image ID and source/dependency verification
update PASS, commit and zero provider calls

future.trigger: Local and remote builds produce different image IDs or toolchains/build metadata change.
future.readonly_check: Compare platform, source commit, all packaged file hashes, dependency inventory and base-image identity before service replacement.
future.preferred_fix: Use a reproducible build or attest the content manifest; keep local/remote image IDs explicitly distinct until parity evidence supports equivalence.
future.stop: Stop if source/dependency/base-image parity cannot be established; image-tag equality alone is insufficient.

incidents.symptom: First MIRACL A POST returned HTTP 200, completed SSE, settled four provider calls with matching usage and finish_reason stop, but controller recorded STEP_NORMAL_API_QUESTION_POST_EXIT_1 / S8_3_WIRE_RESPONSE_INCOMPLETE.
incidents.cause: Stream parser treated the terminal [DONE] frame as sufficient to stop reading and then falsely required transport EOF; it did not wait for EOF after a complete SSE response.
incidents.cause_confidence: high; confirmed by completed saved HTTP/SSE/provider evidence and explicit report
incidents.verified_fix: Strictly require HTTP 200, SETTLED ledger, matching actual usage, finish_reason stop, and final DONE; recover the same run using read-only history/source/DB/wire retrieval. No second question POST or provider call occurred.

evidence.note: read-only recovery completed, provider_calls 0; hash not collected

future.trigger: SSE response contains terminal DONE but client transport remains open or parser reports incomplete wire.
future.readonly_check: Reconcile raw SSE, HTTP status, terminal event, history/source readback, provider ledger settle state, usage and finish reason for the original request ID.
future.preferred_fix: Parse protocol completion independently from socket EOF; keep idempotent no-resend recovery on ambiguous post outcomes.
future.stop: Never repost after POST claim until ledger proves no provider request was sent; preserve response and STOP_NO_RESEND on ambiguity.

incidents.symptom: A stopped retained container was misclassified as active by docker ps -a; subsequent wrapper output filename collision produced a zero-POST tool failure.
incidents.cause: Container existence in all-state listing was conflated with active execution, and wrapper output reused a non-unique filename.
incidents.verified_fix: Preserve the failed zero-POST artifact under a unique zero-post-tool-failures path and continue only unsubmitted cases. Do not repeat any already executed B arm.

evidence.note: preservation operation exit 0; hash not collected
Section 4 documents docker ps -a active misclassification and output filename conflict; no hash recorded

future.trigger: Resume logic sees an existing container or reuses an execution output path.
future.readonly_check: Inspect container State.Running and execution/POST ledger independently; verify output path is absent or uniquely allocated before starting.
future.preferred_fix: Use running-state inspection and collision-resistant per-attempt paths; preserve zero-send failures as immutable evidence.
future.stop: Stop without sending if execution state or output-path ownership is ambiguous; never retry completed arms.

incidents.symptom: All 12 candidate runs lack saved host available-memory minima and container memory peaks; candidate snapshot does not contain OOMKilled evidence.
incidents.cause: The missing measurement is confirmed. Old helper buffered samples in RAM and wrote memory.json only in outer serve finally; Uvicorn 0.35.0 signal handling offers a plausible SIGTERM-before-finally mechanism, but historical signal delivery per container was not recorded.
incidents.cause_confidence: high for NOT_RECORDED gap; partial/inferred for exact loss mechanism
incidents.failed_attempt: Historical minima/peaks unavailable and cannot be backfilled; do not infer no OOM from daily API/Worker status.
incidents.verified_fix: Later diagnostic helper now writes periodic fsynced checkpoints plus atomic snapshots and preserves prior artifacts; offline verification reports 11 tests OK. This fix was not used during the historical real runs.

evidence.note: 12/12 missing; inferred signal mechanism; offline fix evidence
diagnostic tool hash also recorded in results JSON

future.trigger: Long-running candidate execution is terminated, interrupted, or run under a memory cap.
future.readonly_check: Before launch inspect sampler version and output location; during/after run confirm per-case checkpoint journal/snapshot presence and observed timestamps.
future.preferred_fix: Keep durable periodic samples while process is alive; report NOT_RECORDED when samples are missing and keep OOM status separate.
future.stop: Stop interpreting memory or OOM status if historical samples/inspected exit evidence are absent; do not rerun closed authorization to backfill.
